title: Story of the Broke-Back Schoolmaster (മലയാളം)

full_text:
In a bustling ward of Cairo lived a schoolmaster named Master Mansur, who walked with a severe hunch in his back yet possessed the most cheerful disposition in the neighborhood.
The local youths, curious about his curvature, gathered around him one holiday afternoon and asked: 'Master, how came thy back to be bent like a crescent bow?'

Master Mansur chuckled, adjusted his spectacles, and replied:
'Listen, boys, and learn how hasty vanity bows a man's spine!

In my youth, I was tall, vain, and excessively proud of my erect stature. I walked through the markets with my chin held high, looking at the clouds and admiring my own shadow.
One day, the Grand Kazi announced that the chief clerk of his registry had retired, and that the position would be awarded to the candidate of most commanding presence and dignified carriage.

Determined to impress the Kazi, I dressed in a high, stiff turban that added two cubits to my height and walked toward the court building with majestic, haughty strides, refusing to look down at the cobblestones.

As I approached the courthouse entrance, an elderly porter was carrying a massive crate of imported damask fabrics out of a low cellar door. Because my head was held so high in self-admiration, I failed to see the heavy oak beam above the cellar lintel, nor did I see the porter's crate!

I crashed headlong into the oak beam! The impact buckled my knees, and the crate of damask fabrics tumbled from the porter's shoulder directly onto my spine!
When the physicians finally set my bones, my back remained permanently curved in this humble arch.

At first, I wept in bitter despair. But then I realized: before the accident, I was a foolish peacock looking down upon everyone; now, my bowed posture keeps my eyes fixed upon the humble earth where blossoms grow and children play.
My hunch reminds me every day that pride goeth before a fall, and that a bent back that carries knowledge to children is a thousand times better than a straight spine full of arrogance!'

The students laughed, gained deep respect for their teacher, and learned that true dignity lies in the spirit, not the silhouette.
moral: Physical afflictions endured with cheerfulness and patience reflect greater nobility than unblemished folly. [ML]
